originalTitle: Uganda judges push back against lawyers' bid to scrap 'colonial titles'
title: Big Talk in Uganda: How to Talk to Judges!
content:
Hello, my amazing friends! Your friendly news reporter from Africa is here! Today, we're going on a special adventure to a beautiful country called Uganda! It's in East Africa, full of wonderful people, amazing animals like gorillas and elephants, and big lakes. In Uganda, just like everywhere else, there are special places where people go to solve problems and make sure everyone is fair. These places are called **courts**.

Meet the Court Helpers!

In courts, we have very important people. One of them is called a **Judge**. Judges are like super-wise problem-solvers! They wear special long robes, often black, and sit up high to listen to everyone. Their job is to listen carefully to stories and decide what is fair and right. Then we have **Lawyers**. Lawyers are people who help other people tell their stories in court. If someone has a problem, a lawyer helps them explain it to the judge. They are like helpers who know all the rules! Did you know? Lawyers study for many, many years to learn all about the rules and laws! They have to be very smart and good at talking.

A Big Question for Judges

Now, something really interesting is happening in Uganda's courts! The lawyers there are having a big chat about how they talk to judges and show them respect. For a very long time, lawyers have used special words when they talk to a judge. They would say things like, "My Lord" or "My Lady." They also used to bow their heads a little bit when they entered the court or spoke to a judge. These are like special manners or traditions. Just like how you might say "please" and "thank you" or bow your head to an elder to show respect.

Why Some Want Change

Some lawyers are saying, "Hmm, maybe it's time for new manners!" They think that saying "My Lord" or "My Lady" and bowing are very old ways. These ways started a very, very long time ago, when people from other countries ruled Uganda. That time is called the colonial period. It means Uganda was not yet its own boss. The lawyers are saying, "Uganda is a free and independent country now! Maybe we should have our own special ways of showing respect that feel more Ugandan." They want the court to feel like it truly belongs to Uganda today. They think that just saying "Judge" or "Your Honour" (which means "Your Respect") is enough to show respect. And maybe no need to bow. Did you know? Uganda became an independent country on October 9, 1962! That's a long time ago, even before your parents were born!

Why Some Want to Stay the Same

But wait! The judges are also talking about it. Some judges are saying, "These old ways are very important!" They feel that saying "My Lord" or "My Lady" and bowing helps to show how serious and important the court is. It helps everyone remember that the judge's job is very special and needs lots of respect. They believe that these traditions help keep the court a very solemn place where important decisions are made carefully. It makes the court feel special and powerful. It's a way of saying, "When you are in court, you are in a very serious place, and we must all follow special rules." Did you know? The longest river in the world, the River Nile, starts its long journey right here in Uganda! It's super long, flowing all the way to Egypt!

What Happens Next?

So, what's going to happen? Are they going to change or not? Well, it's not a quick decision! Right now, everyone is talking about it. The lawyers are talking, the judges are talking, and probably many other people in Uganda are talking too. They are trying to find the best way forward. A way that shows respect, feels fair, and feels truly Ugandan!

Why This Matters for Uganda

You might be thinking, "Why is how they talk to judges such a big deal?" Well, it's important because it's about how a country decides to show who it is. Every country has its own special ways, its own culture. Uganda is thinking about what traditions it wants to keep from the past and what new traditions it wants to make for the future. It's like deciding what clothes to wear – some old ones you love, some new ones you like! It's a way for Uganda to proudly say, "This is us, and these are our rules, made by us, for us!" Did you know? Uganda is sometimes called the "Pearl of Africa" because it's so beautiful with amazing wildlife and green landscapes!

Stay Tuned!

So, the big chat about courtroom manners is still going on in Uganda. It's a healthy discussion for a country that is always growing and making its own path. Whether they decide to keep "My Lord" or use "Judge," the most important thing is that everyone in court understands the rules and feels respected. We'll keep an eye on this fascinating story and let you know what happens next! Stay curious, my little news explorers!
summary: Lawyers and judges in Uganda are talking about changing old ways of showing respect in court, like saying "My Lord" and bowing, to decide if new Ugandan ways are better.
whyMatters: This is important because Uganda is deciding if it wants to keep old traditions from when other countries ruled or create new ways that truly feel like Uganda today.

originalTitle: Ghanaian influencer extradited to US over $8m scam targeting elderly Americans
title: Be Smart Online! A Story From Ghana
content:
Hello, my super smart friends! It's your friendly news reporter for Africa here, ready to share a very important story with you. Today, we have a story that teaches us about being careful and kind, especially when we use computers or phones. It's about a man from our wonderful continent, Africa, specifically from Ghana, who did something very wrong. But don't worry, we will learn good things from this story and how to stay safe!

A Big Lesson About Being Kind and Careful

This story is like a big lesson from a teacher, but it's a real-life lesson. It tells us that not everyone on the internet is who they say they are. Sometimes, people pretend to be someone nice, but they have a trick up their sleeve. We call this a "scam." A scam is when someone tries to trick you to get something from you, usually money. It's not a game; it's a very serious thing that can hurt people. It's important to know about scams so we can protect ourselves and the people we love. Even though this story is a bit sad because someone did something wrong, it helps us learn how to be super smart and safe when we are online.

Who is Mr. "Big Show"?

There was a man from Ghana. People called him an "influencer." Do you know what an influencer is? It's like someone who is famous on the internet. They share many pictures and videos of themselves. Sometimes they show off nice clothes, big houses, or fancy cars. Many people watch them and follow what they do. Some influencers teach us good things, like how to draw or how to dance, or even how to be kind. But some influencers might show off things that are not good or get things in a bad way. This man was one of those. He loved to show off very expensive things on the internet, on a website called Instagram. He wanted everyone to think he was very rich and successful. **Did you know?** Not all influencers are bad! Many people use the internet to share wonderful art, music, or lessons about our beautiful African cultures. It’s important to choose good people to watch online!

What is a Scam? And What Did He Do?

The man from Ghana was accused of doing a big scam. He tricked many people. He pretended to be someone else online. He made friends with people who lived very far away, in a country called America. These people were often older, like grandmas and grandpas. He would talk to them, send them nice messages, and pretend to be their friend or even someone they loved. This kind of trick is called a "romance scam." It sounds like "love," but it's not real love at all. It's a trick to make people trust you and care about you, so they will do what you ask. Then, after these older people trusted him, he would ask them for money. He would make up sad stories, like "I need money for an emergency" or "I need money to come and visit you." But it was all lies! He just wanted their money for himself. This is very, very wrong, because it takes advantage of people's kindness and trust. **Did you know?** There are many kinds of scams. Some people might pretend to be a prince who needs help, or tell you that you won a big prize, but you need to send money first. Always be careful!

Where Did This Happen?

The people who were tricked lived in a country called America. America is very far away from Ghana. It is across a very big ocean. The man who did the tricking was in Ghana, our lovely African country. The police in America found out about the trick. They knew that many people in their country had lost money because of this man. They wanted to talk to the man. So, something special happened. He was "extradited." This is a big word, but it just means that the government in Ghana helped send him to America. It's like if you did something naughty in another classroom, and your teacher sends you there to explain yourself and face the rules there. He had to travel all the way from Ghana to America so the police there can ask him questions about the trick he played and see if he broke their laws. **Did you know?** Ghana is a beautiful country in West Africa, known for its warm people, delicious jollof rice, and lovely beaches! It's a place where most people are very honest and hardworking, and they believe in doing the right thing.

Who Got Tricked?

The saddest part of this story is that the people who got tricked were often "elderly Americans." This means they were old people, like our grandmas and grandpas. Older people can sometimes be very trusting and kind. They might not know all the tricks that people can play on the internet, especially new tricks that use phones and computers. They just want to make friends or find someone nice to talk to, and they have big, loving hearts. This man took advantage of their kindness and their trusting hearts. He took their hard-earned money. He took more than $8 million from these people! That is a HUGE amount of money. Imagine how hard these grandmas and grandpas worked their whole lives to save that money. **Did you know?** $8 million is so much money! It's enough money to build many, many new schools, or buy thousands of new books for children, or even buy a whole football team many new balls and jerseys! It could help so many people if used for good.

What Did He Do With the Money?

After he tricked these kind, older people and got their money, he didn't use it for good things like helping others or building schools. Instead, he used it to buy very expensive things for himself. He bought fancy cars, big houses, and expensive clothes. And then, he showed all these things off on the internet, on Instagram! He wanted everyone to see how "rich" he was. But this money was not earned honestly. It was money he took from others by tricking them. This is why it is so important to remember that not everything you see online is true or good. Sometimes, what looks fancy is built on something very wrong and hurtful. **Did you know?** Real wealth is not just about how much money you have, but about being kind, honest, and helping others! People who do good things and treat others well are truly rich in spirit.

Why Is This Important For Us?

This story is a very important lesson for all of us, especially you, my smart young friends. Let's remember these important points: 1. **Be careful online:** When you use a phone, tablet, or computer, always remember that not everyone is who they say they are. Some people might not be truthful. 2. **Don't talk to strangers:** Just like we learn not to talk to strangers on the street, it's also important not to talk to strangers online, especially if they ask you for personal information like your address, or your name, or money. 3. **Always tell a grown-up:** If someone online asks you for money, or asks you for your address, or tells you a secret that makes you feel bad, you must tell a trusted grown-up right away. Tell your parents, your teacher, or another family member. They will help you. 4. **Honesty is the best policy:** This man did something dishonest. It brought trouble to him and hurt many people. It is always best to be honest and earn things fairly. Good deeds bring good rewards. 5. **Respect our elders:** We should always respect and protect our grandmas and grandpas. They deserve our love and care, not to be tricked. We should help them if they are confused or need help with new technology. **Did you know?** Your parents and teachers are like your superheroes! They are always there to help and protect you, especially online. Always share your worries with them.

Always Be Kind and Careful!

So, my wonderful friends, let's learn from this story. Let's remember to be kind to everyone, especially our older family members. Let's be smart and careful when we use the internet. The internet can be a wonderful place for learning, playing, and connecting with friends and family, but we must use it wisely. Always remember to ask for help from a grown-up if anything makes you feel worried or confused online. Be safe, be kind, and keep shining bright with your honesty and smart choices!
summary: A man from Ghana is in America because he tricked many old people online to take their money by pretending to be their friend.
whyMatters: This is important because it teaches us to be very careful when we use the internet and to always tell an adult if someone tries to trick us, showing that doing bad things has consequences.

originalTitle: Huge crowds in Mashhad as Iran's late supreme leader is buried
title: A Big Goodbye in Iran: Lots of People Say Farewell to Their Special Leader
content:
Hello from Africa!

Hello, wonderful friends! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here, all the way from sunny Africa! I hope you are having a super day. I am so happy to share some news with you from a country far, far away. This country is called Iran. It is a land with many beautiful mountains and deserts, and kind people live there. Something very important happened in Iran recently. I want to tell you all about it in a simple way. It’s about a very important person and a very big goodbye.

Who Was This Special Leader?

In Iran, there was a very, very important person. He was like the main big boss for the whole country. His name was Ali Khamenei. You can think of him like the head teacher of a very big school, but for a whole country! He was called the 'Supreme Leader.' Being the Supreme Leader means he was the most important leader of all. He helped guide the country and its people for many, many years. When someone so important passes away, people feel very sad, just like when someone special in your family goes to heaven.

A Very Big Goodbye

Sadly, Ali Khamenei passed away. When someone important leaves us, people often have a special way to say goodbye. In Iran, they had a very big goodbye, but it was a sad one. They called these special times 'mourning ceremonies.' These ceremonies went on for six whole days! Can you imagine that? That's a lot of days for people to come together and remember their leader. People all over Iran felt sad, and they wanted to show how much they respected him. It's like when you feel sad for a friend, and you want to give them a hug or write them a card. This was a very big hug from a whole country.

Where Did This Goodbye Happen?

The very last part of this special goodbye happened in a city called Mashhad. It’s a very important city in Iran, like how Accra is important in Ghana, or Lagos in Nigeria. Mashhad is a very special place. And in Mashhad, there is a super special building. It’s called the 'Imam Reza Shrine.' Can you say that with me? Imam Reza Shrine! It is not just a regular building. It is like a very holy church or a very special mosque for people who follow a religion called Islam. Specifically, it's very important for a group called Shia Muslims. This Shrine is like the most sacred and respected place they have in Iran. So, it was a very special place to say a final goodbye to their leader.

So Many People Came!

Can you imagine seeing lots and lots of people, all in one place? Like when everyone comes out for a big parade or a very exciting football match? Well, for Ali Khamenei’s goodbye, there were 'huge crowds.' That means so, so many people! Thousands and thousands of people came to Mashhad. They came from all over Iran, and even from other countries nearby. They wanted to be there to say their last goodbye to their Supreme Leader. They often wore black clothes to show their sadness and respect. It was a sea of people, all sharing their feelings together. It showed how much they respected him and how important he was to them. It was a very powerful sight.

What is a Shrine?

Did you know that a 'shrine' is a very special place? People go to shrines to pray and remember very important holy people or events. These places are often very beautiful inside, with shiny decorations, colorful tiles, and peaceful spaces. It’s a place where people feel very close to their faith.

Different Ways to Say Goodbye

Did you know that saying goodbye to important leaders happens all over the world? Every country has its own special ways of doing it. Some countries might have special music, some might have quiet times for prayer, and some might have big processions. It's a way for everyone to feel together and support each other during a sad time. It shows that even though we live in different places, many human feelings are the same.

Facts About Iran

Did you know that Iran is a very old country in a part of the world called Asia? It has a history that goes back thousands of years! People there have built amazing buildings and created beautiful art for a very long time. People in Iran speak a language called Farsi! It sounds very pretty. They also have lovely gardens and delicious food, like rice with saffron and yummy kebabs. It’s a country full of interesting things!

What Happens Next?

When a very important leader like Ali Khamenei passes away, it means that a new leader will come to guide the country. It's like when your head teacher retires, and a new head teacher takes over the school. The people in Iran will choose or welcome a new Supreme Leader to help guide their country into the future. This is a very big moment for them. It shows that even when sad things happen, life goes on, and new beginnings are always possible. A new chapter for Iran has begun.

A Message from Your Reporter

So, my dear friends, that's the news from Iran today. We learned about a very important leader, a special goodbye ceremony, a very holy place, and lots of people showing their respect. It reminds us that people everywhere care about their leaders and their traditions. It's important to be kind and respectful, no matter where people are from or what their traditions are. We send our thoughts to the people of Iran during this time. This is your African news reporter, signing off! Remember to be curious, be kind, and keep learning new things every day!
summary: People in Iran came together in huge numbers at the Imam Reza Shrine in Mashhad to say their final goodbyes to their very important leader, Ali Khamenei, after six days of mourning.
whyMatters: This is important because Ali Khamenei was the top leader of Iran for a long time, and his goodbye means the country will now welcome a new very important leader to guide them, which is a big change for the people there.
